prompt: A colour photograph is 640 by 416 pixels, with three channels. How many numbers does the file describe?
In shrink.py, what happened when the invoice went from 620 to 310 pixels wide?

choices.text: The error rose from 1.4% to 92.7%
choices.why: Right. At 37 dpi a letter is three or four pixels tall and is no longer there to read.

choices.text: The error stayed under 2%, because Tesseract enlarges small images
choices.why: That is true from 1240 to 620, not below it.

choices.text: Tesseract refused the image as too small
choices.why: It read it and returned text, almost all of it wrong.

choices.text: The error fell, because there was less noise
choices.why: The clean page had no noise to remove; it lost letters.

prompt: Why does the shrink experiment matter when you pay for a vision API?

choices.text: Because smaller images are always read more accurately
choices.why: Below a certain size they are read far worse; the curve has a knee.

choices.text: Because the API refuses images over 1240 pixels wide
choices.why: Nothing in the lesson says so; larger images are accepted and charged for.

choices.text: It finds the smallest size that still reads
choices.why: Right. Pixels beyond it are paid for and add nothing: shrink until the error rises, then step back once.

choices.text: It does not; the API resizes images itself for free
choices.why: It resizes, but it charges by what it reads, and you choose what you send.

prompt: The character error rate counts the characters to change, delete or insert, divided by the length of the ___.
What does Tesseract do before it reads a line?

choices.text: Translates the page into English
choices.why: It does no translation; the language data says which characters to expect.

choices.text: Decides where the text is and in what order to read it
choices.why: Right. Page segmentation comes first, and on the scan it is the step that failed.

choices.text: Asks a vision-language model what the page is
choices.why: Tesseract is a self-contained OCR engine; it calls nothing.

choices.text: Checks the arithmetic of any numbers it finds
choices.why: It reads characters and knows nothing about invoices. The check was extract.py's.

prompt: On the clean invoice, what character error rate did the default page mode (psm 3) give, in percent?
Most of the 24.0% error of psm 3 on the clean page was what?

choices.text: Characters misread because of the font
choices.why: Its characters were almost all right; the same page in psm 6 is 0.4%.

choices.text: Missing accents in São and Brás
choices.why: Those are two characters, and psm 6 in English misses them too at 0.4%.

choices.text: Text read in a different order from the rows
choices.why: Right. The blocks came out one after another instead of row by row.

choices.text: Noise from the scanner
choices.why: This was the clean page, drawn by the lab with no noise.

prompt: Why did `-l eng+por` fix São and Brás?

choices.text: Portuguese data knows the characters ã and á
choices.why: Right. eng has no such characters to read them as.

choices.text: Because Portuguese mode switches to row reading
choices.why: The page mode is set by --psm; the language is a separate setting.

choices.text: Because it translates English titles into Portuguese
choices.why: OCR does not translate. The English titles stayed English.

choices.text: Because two languages double the resolution
choices.why: The image is the same; only the set of expected characters changed.

prompt: In the default mode, the scan's first quantity came back as 2 instead of 12. Why is that dangerous rather than merely wrong?

choices.text: Because 2 is not a valid quantity
choices.why: It is perfectly valid, which is the problem.

choices.text: It looks like a real value
choices.why: Right. Nothing marks it as missing a digit, and a program would order two copies and pay for twelve.

choices.text: Because Tesseract stops reading after a misread
choices.why: It carried on and read the rest of the table.

choices.text: Because it changes the total printed at the bottom of the page
choices.why: The printed total is still 758.50; only the reading of one quantity changed.

prompt: Doubling the scan's size took its error from 0.4% to 1.0%. What does the lesson take from that?

choices.text: Upscaling always harms OCR
choices.why: On another page it could help. The lesson is about measuring, not a new rule.

choices.text: Measure each cure on your own pages
choices.why: Right. A recipe from a tutorial is not your scanner; here enlarging a blur enlarged the blur.

choices.text: Tesseract cannot read images over 1000 pixels wide
choices.why: The clean page is 1240 wide and reads at 0.4%.

choices.text: The scan should have been turned straight first
choices.why: Turning it back changed nothing measurable.

prompt: What does a Tesseract confidence of 86.1 on `713,50` tell you?

choices.text: That 13.9% of its characters are wrong
choices.why: Confidence is not an error rate.

choices.text: That the word is wrong
choices.why: The same list held 10 and Palmeiras, both right.

choices.text: That the word is worth checking
choices.why: Right. A hint about where to look, not a verdict.

choices.text: That the number is a total, which Tesseract scores lower
choices.why: Tesseract knows nothing about totals.

prompt: Which check caught `15.96` in the English-only reading of the scan?

choices.text: Quantity times unit price must equal the line's amount
Tesseract's confidence for the word
choices.why: It scored 61.6, but Palmeiras, which is right, scored 24.4: a hint, not a catch.

choices.text: The lines must add up to the subtotal
choices.why: The amount column was read right, so the sum still agreed.

choices.text: Subtotal plus shipping must make the total
choices.why: Those three were read right.

prompt: Why is the invoice's arithmetic a better check than asking a second, similar model to read it?

choices.text: Arithmetic is faster to run
choices.why: True, and not the reason. Speed does not make a check right.

choices.text: A second model is not allowed to read the same image
choices.why: Nothing forbids it. It is just less independent.

choices.text: Arithmetic catches every possible error
choices.why: It missed Bras Cubas, which no sum depends on.

choices.text: It is exact and does not depend on the model
choices.why: Right. A similar model on the same blur is exposed to the same mistake.

prompt: The title came back as Bras Cubas and every check passed. Which structure would catch it?

choices.text: Marginalia's own catalogue of books
choices.why: Right. The closest title in books.jsonl is The Posthumous Memoirs of Brás Cubas.

choices.text: A higher Tesseract confidence threshold for every word on the page
choices.why: Confidence is a hint and would also flag correct words.

choices.text: The subtotal
choices.why: No sum depends on a title.

choices.text: Reading the page in mode 3 instead of mode 6
choices.why: Mode 3 also wrote Bras, and scrambled the rows.

prompt: Put extract.py's steps in the order the program runs them.
items: match each row against the line pattern
turn every amount into integer cents
print the data and the verdict

prompt: What three things does an object detector return for each object?

choices.text: A caption, a language and a confidence
choices.why: A caption is a VLM's output; a detector returns a label from a list.

choices.text: A box, a label and a score
choices.why: Right. Where, what, and how sure.

choices.text: A mask, a colour and a size in bytes
choices.why: Masks are a segmentation model's output, not this detector's.

choices.text: The text inside it, its position and its font
choices.why: That is closer to OCR's TSV.

prompt: How many classes can the lab's EfficientDet-Lite0 detector name?
Why did the detector call the invoice `book`?

choices.text: It read the titles of the four books on it
choices.why: A detector does not read text.

choices.text: Its list has no class for a document
choices.why: Right. So it named the closest thing it knows: a closed vocabulary does not know that it does not know.

choices.text: The invoice image is a photograph of a book
choices.why: It was drawn by the lab: text and lines on white.

choices.text: It is 51% likely to be a book
choices.why: A score is the model's evidence, not a probability of being right.

prompt: A team wants to blur every face in customer photos before storing them. Which tool fits, according to the lesson?

choices.text: A vision-language model asked to describe the faces
choices.why: A sentence about faces gives no pixels to blur, and it sends the faces out to describe them.

choices.text: A detector, which returns where each face is and runs on the machine
choices.why: Right. Geometry, speed and nothing leaving the machine.

choices.text: OCR, which finds the regions of the image with content
choices.why: OCR finds text, not faces.

choices.text: None; faces cannot be found without identifying the person
choices.why: Finding where a face is and knowing whose it is are different jobs.

prompt: What is the defining difference between a vision-language model and the detector?

choices.text: A VLM is always more accurate
choices.why: It is also the one most able to invent.

choices.text: No fixed list
choices.why: Right. It answers in an open vocabulary: invoice, cover or anything else.

choices.text: A VLM runs on the device
choices.why: The detector is the one that runs on a phone. VLMs are mostly called over an API.

choices.text: A VLM returns boxes with every answer
choices.why: Geometry is the detector's strength.

prompt: The course's illustrative description calls the cover's dark rectangle a building. What kind of claim is that?

choices.text: A misread of text on the cover
choices.why: There is no text there to misread.

choices.text: A fact any OCR would confirm
choices.why: OCR reads letters, not shapes.

choices.text: A hallucinated barcode
choices.why: That is the plausible-addition error; a building is a reading of what is there.

choices.text: An interpretation of shapes
choices.why: Right. The drawing is rectangles; building is the reader's story, fine in a description and wrong in an extraction.

prompt: Which of these prompts produce output you can verify? Choose every one that applies.

choices.text: List every piece of text on the cover, exactly as written
choices.why: Right. OCR on the same image checks it.

choices.text: Describe the mood of the cover
choices.why: There is no single right answer to check against.

choices.text: Return the invoice's lines and total as JSON
choices.why: Right. The arithmetic checks it.

choices.text: Say whether this cover would sell well
choices.why: An opinion, not a checkable fact.

prompt: A supplier sends invoices as PDFs with a text layer. What should read them?

choices.text: A vision-language model, for the layout
choices.why: The text is already in the file.

choices.text: No model: read the text layer
choices.why: Right. Exact and free.

choices.text: Tesseract in row mode
choices.why: That re-reads a picture of text that was already text.

choices.text: A detector, to find the table first
choices.why: Its list has no table class.

prompt: What does "cheap first, expensive on doubt" mean for the invoices?

choices.text: Use the cheapest VLM and switch to a better one if it is slow
choices.why: Speed is not the trigger; a failed check is.

choices.text: OCR and checks first; only failures go further
choices.why: Right. Only pages that fail go to a VLM or a person, so on clean suppliers the expensive path almost never runs.

choices.text: Read every page twice and keep the cheaper reading
choices.why: Cost is not how you pick between readings; checks are.

choices.text: Start with small images and enlarge until the model is sure
choices.why: Confidence is not proof, and enlarging was measured to hurt here.

prompt: Match each job to the tool the lesson's table gives it.
A new supplier's scans read at 3% CER in psm 6, and every arithmetic check passes on 50 invoices. One day a check fails. What should the pipeline do with that invoice?

choices.text: Accept it, since 50 earlier ones passed
choices.why: The check exists for this one.

choices.text: Retry OCR with the same settings until the check passes
choices.why: The same model on the same image gives the same reading.

choices.text: Send it down the expensive path: a VLM or a person
choices.why: Right. A failed check is exactly the doubt the expensive path is for.

choices.text: Drop the amounts and keep the titles
choices.why: The amounts are what the stock system needs most.

prompt: You must read shelf labels in a warehouse photographed by phone. Labels are printed and always in the same template, but photos are taken at angles. Which plan follows the lesson?

choices.text: Find the label, crop it, OCR it, then check codes against the stock list
choices.why: Right. Detector for where, OCR for what, and the stock list as the independent check.

choices.text: A VLM for every photo, because angles defeat OCR
choices.why: Possibly for the photos where the cheap path fails, but not first.

choices.text: Tesseract psm 3 on the whole photo
choices.why: The whole photo is mostly shelves; the label has to be found first.

choices.text: Enlarge every photo twice before OCR
choices.why: Enlarging was measured to hurt on the scan; it is not a default.
